title: CUDA image processing
highlights: Radial brightening: three kernels compared, a floating-point baseline, an integer version using bit shifts, and a version that precomputes one multiplier per block in shared memory.
Compositing: pastes one image onto another at a chosen position, one thread per pixel.
Region analysis: red-channel analysis and red-dominant region detection, with threads updating shared results.
BMP and PNG input (libpng), a Makefile build, and a command-line interface per operation.
summary: A CUDA image-processing toolkit for BMP and PNG files: radial brightening, image compositing, red-region detection and bounding-box extraction. Three brightening kernels are compared on execution time. Built for a GPU programming course.

details.label: Pipeline
details.body: Images are read from BMP or PNG (libpng handles PNG), copied to the GPU, processed by an operation-specific kernel, and written back to BMP. Each operation is selected from the command line, for example compositing takes a second image and an X/Y position, and the program reports the run time of the kernel.

details.label: Radial brightening
details.body: Each pixel is brightened by its distance from the image centre, up to a 2.0 multiplier. Three kernels implement it so the cost of each design choice shows up in the timings. The baseline computes a floating-point factor per pixel. The second maps the distance to a scaled integer and multiplies with bit shifts, which are cheaper on a GPU. The third computes one multiplier per block into a shared array before the main kernel runs, so threads in a block reuse it, with a barrier so no thread writes its result early.

details.label: Compositing and region analysis
details.body: The compositing kernel replaces the pixels of the main image that fall inside the placed image's rectangle and writes the result to a separate output buffer. The analysis kernels measure the red channel, flag red-dominant pixels, and update shared results, from which bounding boxes are extracted for each detected region.

details.label: CPU side
details.body: The repository also holds a pthread merge sort (65,536 integers sorted in 1K chunks, merged in doubling passes, with a mutex handing chunks to threads) from the same course.
